claim: The new `section DivisionMonoid` in Finset/Basic.lean declares three `variable` lines that each repeat `[DivisionMonoid α] … [DecidableEq α] {s t : Finset α}`. The third, after `end RightCancel`, re-declares exactly the `LeftCancel` variables. Each line serves a single lemma, and the outer `section DivisionMonoid` declares nothing itself. The sub-sections are also named `LeftCancel`/`RightCancel`, unlike the neighbouring `section IsLeftCancelMul`/`section IsRightCancelMul` (lines 1147, 1184).
requested_change:
Declare the shared variables once and bind each cancellation mixin in the signature that uses it:
section DivisionMonoid
variable [DivisionMonoid α] [DecidableEq α] {s t : Finset α}

@[to_additive] lemma card_le_card_div_left [IsLeftCancelMul α] (hs : s.Nonempty) : #t ≤ #(s / t) :=
  have ⟨_, ha⟩ := hs; card_le_card_image₂_left _ ha div_right_injective

@[to_additive] lemma card_le_card_div_right [IsRightCancelMul α] (ht : t.Nonempty) :
    #s ≤ #(s / t) :=
  have ⟨_, ha⟩ := ht; card_le_card_image₂_right _ ha div_left_injective

@[to_additive] lemma card_le_card_div_self [IsLeftCancelMul α] : #s ≤ #(s / s) := by
  cases s.eq_empty_or_nonempty <;> simp [card_le_card_div_left, *]

end DivisionMonoid
(Alternatively, keep the outer variable line and use sub-sections `IsLeftCancelMul` (holding card_le_card_div_left and card_le_card_div_self) and `IsRightCancelMul` that add only `variable [IsLeftCancelMul α]` / `variable [IsRightCancelMul α]`.)

claim: The description says 'I have no intended use for these generalizations; they are proposed for their own sake'. It names no structure that is a `DivInvMonoid` with `IsRightCancelMul`, or a `DivisionMonoid` with `IsLeftCancelMul`, without being a `Group`. Meanwhile the PR replaces the single assumption `[Group G]` with two-class assumptions in three files, so the benefit is not evident to a reviewer. Such a structure exists mathematically (verified: in a DivisionMonoid left cancellation already gives right cancellation, and e.g. (ℕ, +) with `-a := a` is a cancellative subtraction monoid that is not a group), but the PR does not say whether Mathlib has an instance.
